sources.researchNote: Paris Musées explicitly credits Neurdein Frères as “éditeur” and dates the object only to the twentieth century. It does not identify an individual photographer or establish the former 1900–1933 range. No exact creation or printing year is adopted here. Paris Musées Collections is the access platform, not the original publisher; the inventory’s acquisition date of 20 December 2021 does not date the postcard.

media.title: Rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris — historical postcard
media.description: Undated postcard view of rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in the Plaine Monceau quarter of Paris, catalogued by Musée Carnavalet as twentieth century. It provides street context for the Polish Consulate General, located at number 19 in the late 1920s and 1930s; the postcard does not establish that the consulate building itself is visible.
media.altText: Postcard showing rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in Paris, lined with town houses, with horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians.
media.publicCaption: Rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Plaine Monceau, Paris. Undated postcard; museum dating: twentieth century. The Polish Consulate General was located at number 19 in the late 1920s and 1930s.
